newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close up on blue-chip earnings.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close up on blue-chip earnings.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished higher on Friday on buying of blue chip shares reporting solid earnings in the first three quarters, brokers said.
The weighted index ended up 29.02 points or 0.45 percent at 6,455.11, but off an intraday peak of 6,476.91. Turnover was T$41.05 billion. The market was closed on Thursday for holiday.

Electronic shares with good earnings led Friday's gain, rising 1.37 percent. The most active issue, First International Computer advanced T$1.8 or 4.57 percent to T$41.2. Taiwan Liton jumped T$2.4 or 5.7 percent to T$44.5.
"Today's buying in electronics are selective. It only concentrates on firms that showed sound profits," said Tank Hung, an analyst of Yuan Ta Securities.

"Overall Sentiment is not good enough to push up the index to challenge a higher level," Hung said. Many electronics firms have said they expected to do better in the fourth quarter because it is the traditional strong business season.

The heavily weighted financials rose 0.75 percent, but previous gainers plastics and textiles were down on profit-taking. Formosa Chemical Fibre lost 10 cents or 0.3 percent to T$33.3 on active trade.

Kee Tai Properties, a construction investment firm, soared by the daily seven percent limit. It was up T$2.1 to T$32.5 on what brokers called a "honeymoon rally" on its first day of listing in the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
Shipping firm Yang Ming Marine was up T$1.3 or 4.35 percent to T$31.2.

Brokers said they expected the market to consolidate at around current levels on Saturday, adding investors would remain cautious as the index approaches the 6,500-point barrier. -- Alice Hung (2-5080815)
